draft.title: Radians
card: On a unit circle (radius 1), the angle at the centre in radians equals the arc length it cuts off. So an arc of length 1 gives an angle of 1 radian.
The unit circle has circumference 2π, so a full turn is 2π radians. This means π radians = 180°.
on a circle of radius r, arc length = radius × angle in radians, so l = rθ. Example: r = 4 and θ = π/3 give l = 4π/3.
degrees × π/180 gives radians. Radians × 180/π gives degrees. Example: 60° × π/180 = π/3.
draft.remember: π radians is 180°. Use π/180 to go to radians and 180/π to go to degrees.

a.why: 150 × π/180 = 150π/180 = 5π/6. The option 6π/5 turns the fraction upside down, which would come from using 180/150 instead of 150/180.
a.clue: Multiply by π/180, then simplify the fraction.

b.q: A dial is turned through 5π/4 radians. What is this angle in degrees?
b.why: 5π/4 × 180/π = 5 × 45 = 225°. The option 150° comes from using 5π/6, a different fraction, and 240° is 4π/3, so neither fits 5π/4.
b.clue: Multiply by 180/π so that π cancels.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 150° is 5π/6 and 5π/4 radians is 225°. The card's facts and examples are correct.
